answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by staking a unique hardware fingerprint: each node must present a cryptographic attestation burned into its silicon, much like an opal's fixed fire inside stone. Attempts to spawn fake identities then shatter against this seal, because one chip cannot be split into many. Verification becomes a mirror in which every account reflects its single physical origin. Meanwhile, the ledger ages each credential like a glacier, slowly grinding away stale claims until only genuine actors remain.
